what_it_is.value: Wave Terminal is an open-source, AI-integrated desktop terminal (Electron front end, Go backend) whose tabs are tiled 'blocks'. Each block holds one widget: an xterm.js terminal, a file/directory preview, a code editor, a web browser, sysinfo, or Wave AI. The `wsh` CLI, available in every terminal block, opens previews (`wsh view`), editors (`wsh edit`) and web blocks (`wsh web open`) beside the terminal.
what_it_is.note: [measured] read wsh-reference.mdx (view/edit/web sections) and docs/tabs.mdx ('The tabs are comprised of tiled blocks. The contents of each block is a single widget') this session.

language.note: [measured] languages endpoint; Electron version from package.json ("electron": "^41.1.0").

graphics_mechanism.value: Everything is Electron DOM. Terminal blocks are xterm.js 6 with the WebGL or DOM renderer. Web blocks are Electron <webview> tags (WebviewTag, per-block partition). Preview blocks route by MIME type to React renderers: react-markdown for Markdown, plus specialised views for image, video, audio and PDF, and a streaming view for media. The terminal has no image protocol: there is no @xterm/addon-image in package.json, and 'Support a graphics protocol' (sixel/kitty/iTerm) is issue #2172, open since 2025-05-17.
graphics_mechanism.note: [measured] preview-model.tsx mime checks (application/pdf, video/, audio/, image/, text/markdown); webview.tsx imports WebviewTag; package.json xterm addons = fit, search, serialize, web-links, webgl only; issue #2172 read via gh api.

where_it_draws.value: Split pane. Each preview, web or editor view is a tile ('block') in the tab's tiling layout, created beside the terminal. Blocks can be dragged to re-dock, and 'magnified' (Cmd+M) to fill the tab over the others, the nearest thing Wave has to a floating panel. Nothing is drawn inline in terminal scrollback, so nothing scrolls with text.
where_it_draws.note: [measured] tabs.mdx 'Tab Layout System' (drag blocks by header, resize nodes, 'Magnify a block'); wsh view -m 'opens in magnified block'.

input_model.value: Block focus model: click, or Ctrl+Shift+arrows/hjkl/1-9, moves focus between blocks, and the focused block receives keys. In web blocks Cmd+L focuses the URL bar and Escape hands focus to the page. Wave ships a dedicated 'Refocus the current block' key (Cmd+I, 'useful if the block has lost input focus'), which tells you embedded content does steal focus. In terminal blocks, links activate only on Cmd+click (macOS) or Ctrl+click (Linux/Windows).
input_model.note: [measured] keybindings.mdx table; modifier check read in frontend/app/view/term/termwrap.ts (WebLinksAddon handler: metaKey on macOS, ctrlKey elsewhere).

td_overlap.note: [inferred] open-on-click covers URLs only: openLink() creates a 'web' block when web:openlinksinternally is set, otherwise opens the external browser; file paths are not linkified. host-protocol here is the wsh CLI/RPC, not a graphics escape. agent-panes: Claude Code tab badges via hooks + `wsh badge` (docs/docs/claude-code.mdx).

steal_for_td.value: Give Ctrl+click and a CLI the same verb: `td view [-m] [-r <pane>] <path>` over TD's ctl socket, with one resolver that picks the renderer by MIME type (Markdown, image, PDF, video, directory). `-m` opens the result as the floating square; `-r` replaces an existing preview pane instead of adding another split. Wave's `wsh view -m` and `wsh web open -r <blockid>` are this pair, minus the click.
steal_for_td.note: [inferred] analysis; flags -m/--magnified and -r/--replace are measured from wsh-reference.mdx ('--replace and --magnified cannot be used together').

trap.value: Wave never linkified file paths in terminal output. Only URLs go through its WebLinksAddon, so a good preview system is reachable only by typing `wsh view`. Its terminal also has no graphics protocol (#2172). The click is the feature: don't ship the preview pane without the path detector.
trap.note: [inferred] from termwrap.ts (the only link provider is WebLinksAddon; no registerLinkProvider for paths found by gh code search) and issue #2172. Absence of path links is a code-search result, not a statement by the project.

what_it_is.value: Terminology is the EFL (Enlightenment) terminal. Clicking a link to an image, video or Edje file pops the media up inside the terminal window. Its ty* helpers drive the same machinery from the shell over a private 'ESC } ... NUL' escape protocol: tycat (inline), typop (popup), tyq (queue), tybg (background), tyls (listing with thumbnails).
what_it_is.note: [measured] README companion tools + extended escapes; click-to-popup path read in src/bin/termio.c _activate_link().

license.note: [measured] gh api reports NOASSERTION; COPYING opens 'Copyright notice for Terminology (BSD 2-Clause License)'.

language.value: C (~1.45 MB) on EFL/Elementary, Meson build

graphics_mechanism.value: Native EFL canvas (Evas, optionally OpenGL). The terminal's own escapes carry a local file path or URL, not pixels. `pn`/`pq` pop up media now or queued. `is`/`ic`/`if`/`it` reserve a WxH cell area, filled with a chosen 'replace character' between `ib`/`ie` markers, and draw the media over those cells: stretched, centred, filled, or as a cached thumbnail with a click-through link. `ij` embeds a live Edje object that can send signals back on stdin. No sixel ('Sixel/ReGIS Graphics Attributes: TODO' in termptyesc.c) and no Kitty graphics.
graphics_mechanism.note: [measured] README escape table; termptyesc.c grep for sixel/kitty.

where_it_draws.value: Two ways. Popups (a click, typop, or `pn`) are a floating layer swallowed into the theme's 'terminology.popmedia' part over the terminal, with image, scale, edje and movie variants. Escape closes it, and hover-link detection pauses while it's up. Inline media (tycat, `is` and friends) is cell-anchored over placeholder characters in the grid, so it scrolls with the text.

input_model.value: The inverse of TD's plan. With helper.inline_please on, a plain click on a media link pops it up inside Terminology, and Ctrl+click skips the popup and runs the external helper (xdg-open, or a per-type command for image, video or general). Link activation waits 0.2 s so a double-click can cancel it. Unknown URLs get an HTTP HEAD (2.5 s timeout) to learn their type first. Links that arrived via OSC 8 escapes are gated by a separate setting (active_links_escape).

Image data arrives by one of four transmission mediums: direct in the escape (t=d), a file path (t=f), a temp file (t=t) or POSIX shared memory (t=s). Images are uploaded once by id and then placed as placements with z-index; negative z draws under text, and below INT32_MIN/2 also under non-default cell backgrounds. Also supported: relative placements (P=/Q= parent), client- and terminal-driven animation (a=f frames, since 0.20.0), and Unicode placeholders, where the codepoint U+10EEEE carries the image id in its foreground colour and diacritics carry the row and column, so images survive tmux and vim. kitty has no Sixel support. what_it_is.value: Arcan is a display server and 'desktop engine': a Lua-scripted multimedia engine plus the SHMIF IPC and TUI API, which aims to replace terminal escape protocols altogether. Durden is its tiling/stacking desktop. Cat9 is a Lua user shell for Lash (Arcan's TUI command line) in which every command becomes a tracked job whose output can be folded, reused, popped out as a window or, through `open`, embedded as media (image, PDF, video) decoded by a separate afsrv_decode process into a clipped region of the shell's own window.

The 2017 design post lists 'Crazy encoding schemes for representing non-character data – such as Sixel' among the problems TUI replaces.

what_it_is.value: Native macOS terminal app (Swift/AppKit; terminal rendering via libghostty) built for running many coding agents. It has a vertical-tab sidebar with branch, PR, ports and notification text, notification rings on panes that need attention, and non-terminal panes beside terminals: a WKWebView browser pane, a live-reloading Markdown viewer and File Preview panels, opened by Cmd-click on paths and links or by `cmux markdown open plan.md` / `cmux open`.
what_it_is.note: [measured] README, skills/cmux-markdown/SKILL.md, CHANGELOG.md.

license.value: GPL-3.0-or-later (LICENSE file; GitHub reports NOASSERTION because of a commercial-terms preamble)
license.note: [measured] spdx NOASSERTION; LICENSE text: 'licensed under the GNU General Public License v3.0 or later (GPL-3.0-or-later)'.

language.value: Swift (87.6 MB) dominant; also Rust 18.7 MB, TypeScript 13.2 MB, Python 10.3 MB, Zig 1.2 MB (libghostty)

graphics_mechanism.value: Native GPU terminal via libghostty ('the same way apps use WebKit for web views') plus embedded web views: the Markdown viewer was 'Rewritten… with a webview-based renderer' (#3664; Resources/markdown-viewer/shell.html; tables, Mermaid, inline images), and browser panes are WKWebView (Sources/Panels/WKWebView+*.swift) with a scriptable agent-browser API. Whether terminal panes accept Kitty graphics from programs was not verified.
graphics_mechanism.note: [measured] CHANGELOG (#3664), README ('Powered by libghostty'), gh code search hits for WKWebView under Sources/Panels.

where_it_draws.value: split pane: `cmux markdown open` 'opens as a horizontal split to the right of the source surface'; Cmd+Shift+L opens a browser in a split; panels are tabs in the split tree and are restored across sessions (the Markdown panel re-reads the file from disk and is not recreated if the file is gone). Not inline in scrollback; no separate OS window.
where_it_draws.note: [measured] commands.md 'Panel behavior', README shortcuts table.

input_model.value: Cmd-click on terminal text routes by type: Markdown paths → Markdown viewer (#4864; first an opt-in setting, #2904), HTML files → browser pane (#9096), other supported files → cmux (#4041), URLs → the built-in browser, including inside fullscreen TUIs like Claude Code and Codex (#5406) and OSC 8 links (#3580). Viewer and browser panes take native AppKit focus (Cmd+F find, zoom). Everything is scriptable over the CLI and a Unix socket.
input_model.note: [measured] CHANGELOG entries cited by PR number.

td_overlap.note: [inferred] The closest shipped match to TD's feature: Cmd-click a .md/.html path → viewer pane beside the terminal. Not same-stack (Swift + libghostty), no floating squares found.

steal_for_td.value: Ship the viewer as a live-reloading pane that agents can open, not only people. `cmux markdown open plan.md` splits a Markdown panel to the right, re-renders on every write (atomic saves handled), and cmux tells agents in AGENTS.md to write the whole plan first and then open it. TD should expose the same route as Ctrl+click through a `td open <path>` CLI (or OSC request) with file watching, so an agent's plan, brief or HTML report appears beside its pane and stays current.
steal_for_td.note: [inferred] From SKILL.md ('Write the full plan file first, then open it, so the panel never shows a partially written file'). Fits Parker's existing 'Deliverable:' line convention, which already names the file an agent wants opened.

trap.value: Click-to-open detection is where the bugs live. cmux's changelog shows Markdown paths with trailing punctuation detected as URLs (#4594), Cmd-click failing on soft-wrapped URLs (#8110), clicks swallowed inside fullscreen TUIs that capture the mouse (#5406), OSC 8 Cmd-click broken (#3580), a recursive-lock crash on the Markdown route (#3559), and blank Markdown viewers after resize or being dragged to another column (#10474, #6331). TD should match paths on the logical (unwrapped) line with punctuation trimming, honour Ctrl+click even when the app has mouse reporting on, and keep viewer state alive across re-parenting.
trap.note: [inferred] Lesson from measured CHANGELOG entries.

primary_sources.note: [measured] Read via gh api on 2026-09-24. cmux is a terminal app, so cluster A may also claim it.

updates.label: Claude Squad — agent sessions on tmux + worktrees
updates.group: C · Multiplexers and TUI-as-window-manager

what_it_is.value: Go TUI (`cs`) that manages several terminal agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Aider, …), each in its own tmux session and git worktree: an instance list on the left, a live preview tab and a diff tab on the right, Enter to attach full-screen, commit/push and pause/resume per instance. Text only.
what_it_is.note: [measured] README 'How It Works': tmux sessions, git worktrees, 'A simple TUI interface'.

language.value: Go (263 KB): bubbletea v1.3.4, lipgloss, creack/pty

graphics_mechanism.value: none — text cells only. The preview tab is `tmux capture-pane -p -e -J` output (ANSI kept, wrapped lines joined) re-rendered inside a lipgloss box; status detection re-captures the pane and compares content / looks for prompts (HasUpdated).
graphics_mechanism.note: [measured] session/tmux/tmux.go:476-478 CapturePaneContent, ui/preview.go.

where_it_draws.value: split inside its own TUI (list | tabbed preview/diff window); attaching replaces the whole terminal with `tmux attach-session` through a PTY (fullscreen) until Ctrl-q.
where_it_draws.note: [measured] tmux.go Attach/Restore (exec tmux attach-session via ptyFactory), README menu.

input_model.value: Bubbletea key handling: n / N new (with prompt), ↑/↓ or j/k select, Tab switches preview↔diff, shift-↑/↓ scrolls the diff, Enter/o attaches (keys then go straight to the agent through the attached PTY), Ctrl-q detaches back to the list.
input_model.note: [measured] README Menu section.

td_overlap.note: [inferred] Agent multiplexer on tmux + worktrees; no floating, no graphics.

steal_for_td.value: A read-only peek: selecting an agent in the list shows its live screen in a side panel without moving focus, and Tab flips the same panel to that worktree's diff; Enter commits to a full attach. TD can offer this as a floating square: hover or select a pane in the sidebar to peek at its live grid, Tab for its git diff, Enter to focus. The floating square then shows other panes as well as files.
steal_for_td.note: [inferred] From README navigation and ui/preview.go.

trap.value: Don't build the peek from re-captured text. claude-squad polls `capture-pane` and re-renders the ANSI inside lipgloss, which drops anything that isn't cells (no images), costs a subprocess per refresh, and has mangled wide characters (#233, 'Chinese/Unicode characters display as garbled text'). TD holds every pane's alacritty_terminal grid in-process, so a peek should render that grid (and its image placements) directly.
trap.note: [inferred] From tmux.go capture path and issue #233 title (closed); root cause of #233 not read.

updates.label: twin — text-mode window environment
updates.group: C · Multiplexers and TUI-as-window-manager

what_it_is.value: A text-mode windowing environment that 'implements in text mode the same concepts that X11 does in graphics': overlapping, draggable, resizable windows with per-window menus and gadgets, virtual screens, a built-in window manager and truecolor terminal emulator, networked clients (libtw) and displays that attach and detach on the fly (twdisplay). Runs on the Linux console, in X11, in a tty, or nested in itself.
what_it_is.note: [measured] README and docs/Tutorial section 1 'Concepts'.

license.value: GPL-2.0 (server and clients); libtutf and libtw are LGPL
license.note: [measured] spdx GPL-2.0; README 'COPYING.LIB' note for the libraries.

graphics_mechanism.value: none — text cells only. Under X11 twin opens its own window and draws the cell grid (Xft build dependency); no image protocol appears in README or Tutorial.
graphics_mechanism.note: [measured] README display list and build deps; absence of image support is [inferred] from README/Tutorial greps, not a source audit.

where_it_draws.value: floating (overlapping) windows in a cell grid with raise/lower stacking and maximize; virtual screens up to ~64K cells, scrolled by dragging to the screen edge; window contents may exceed the window and scroll.
where_it_draws.note: [measured] Tutorial 1.c-1.e.

input_model.value: The built-in WM 'does window focus changes, window drags and resizes, virtual screen changes, menu activity and dispatches keystrokes and mouse events to the focused window'. PAUSE or the right mouse button opens the focused window's menu; its Window item offers Move, Resize, Scroll, Center, Maximize, Raise/Lower and a Window List. On generic ttys the mouse works only with xterm-style reporting.
input_model.note: [measured] Tutorial sections 1-2 and the menu walkthrough (~lines 270-321).

activity.note: [measured] repo metadata and releases/latest (README header still says 0.9.1).

td_overlap.note: [inferred] Overlapping draggable windows inside a text environment; no graphics, no agents.

steal_for_td.value: Make floating squares fully keyboard-operable and listable, not mouse-only. twin puts Move, Resize, Center, Maximize, Raise/Lower on every window's menu and keeps a Window List that focuses and centres the chosen window. TD's draggable square should likewise have a keyboard move/resize mode, snap-to-centre / maximize-within-pane, and a list of open squares; tmux 3.7 shipped floating panes mouse-only and had to add keyboard move/resize in 3.8.
steal_for_td.note: [inferred] From twin's Tutorial menu section and tmux CHANGES 3.7/3.8.

trap.value: A window manager built out of cells inherits cell limits: twin windows can hold only text, geometry snaps to the character grid, and on generic ttys mouse handling depends on the host's reporting ('it may have problems with mouse (only xterm and derivatives have a standard to report mouse)'). TD's floating square should be a gpui layer with pixel geometry and native input, placed over the terminal grid, not a window emulated inside it.
trap.note: [inferred] From Tutorial section 2 'Supported displays'.

what_it_is.value: Überzug++: a C++ daemon, drop-in replacement for the defunct ueberzug. Host programs (lf, yazi, vifm, ranger, fzf scripts, image.nvim) send it JSON add/remove commands over stdin or a unix socket, and it paints a raster image (including GIF and animated WebP) into a column/row box. It renders no documents, only images.
what_it_is.note: [measured] README read via gh api on 2026-09-24.

language.value: C++ (about 93% of bytes), plus CMake and Shell

graphics_mechanism.value: Six backends, selected by -o or config.json: x11 and wayland (a separate borderless, unfocusable compositor window per image, placed over the terminal), and kitty, sixel, iterm2, chafa (escape sequences written to the terminal). Escape-code probing is OFF by default (--use-escape-codes [0]). By default it reads TIOCGWINSZ for pixel size, marks iterm2 from TERM_PROGRAM (WezTerm, iTerm.app), and marks x11/wayland available from the session. Detection is last-wins in the order sixel < kitty < iterm2 < x11 < wayland, with chafa if nothing is found. So on Hyprland it picks the overlay window even inside a kitty-capable terminal. With probing on, it sends `ESC_Gi=31,s=1,v=1,a=q,t=d,f=24;AAAA ESC\ CSI c` (kitty), `CSI ?1;1;0S` (XTSMGRAPHICS sixel), and `CSI 14t` then `CSI ?2;1;0S` for pixel size.
graphics_mechanism.note: [measured] Read in src/terminal.cpp (set_detected_output, check_kitty_support, check_sixel_support) and src/canvas.cpp.

where_it_draws.value: With the wayland and x11 backends, it draws an overlay OS window positioned over cells. On Hyprland it sets window rules by title over the Hyprland IPC socket (float, no_focus, border_size 0, rounding 0), probing for the new Lua IPC first. It then moves the window to activewindow.at + col×font_width + guessed padding. It knows pane offsets only for tmux (tmux::get_offset). The window does not scroll with text; the host must send `remove`. With the kitty, sixel and iterm2 backends, it writes a cell-anchored placement to the terminal's stdout instead.
where_it_draws.note: [measured] Also read src/canvas/wayland/window/waylandshm.cpp (move_window) and src/dimensions.cpp (read_offsets).

input_model.value: It has no input of its own and takes no keys or mouse. The host TUI owns input and sends JSON `{action:add|remove, identifier, path, x, y, max_width, max_height}` in columns and lines, over stdin or ${UEBERZUGPP_TMPDIR}/ueberzugpp-${PID}.socket. The overlay window gets no_focus, so it never takes keyboard focus.
input_model.note: [measured] no_focus rule seen in hyprland.cpp disable_focus().

td_overlap.note: [inferred] Its Wayland/X11 backend puts a floating image square over a pane. TD wants the same result, but drawn in-process. It is a client program, not a host, and it is C++, so not same-stack.

steal_for_td.value: Report exact per-pane pixel sizes in TIOCGWINSZ: ws_xpixel/ws_ypixel should equal cols×cell width and rows×cell height of the pane, not of the window. Also answer CSI 14t for the pane. Ueberzugpp derives font size and padding from these numbers, and its guess_padding() computes zero padding only when the pixels divide exactly by cols. mcat, tdf and w3m read the same fields.
steal_for_td.note: [inferred] From get_terminal_size() and guess_padding() in terminal.cpp.

trap.value: Nothing should fall back to overlay windows inside TD. The Wayland backend positions against the whole Hyprland client window plus guessed padding, and it knows nothing about TD's own splits. Whenever monitor scale is above 1 it halves coordinates and adds 10 px (`res_x/2 + 10`), which is only right at 2×. Issues for wrong position and scale on Hyprland/Sway (#122) and wrong workspace (#223) are still open. And because it prefers wayland over kitty, a user with ueberzugpp installed gets overlay windows unless the host program detects TD's graphics first.
trap.note: [inferred] Scale hack read in hyprland.cpp move_window(). Issue states from gh search on 2026-09-24: #122 open (2023-08-26), #223 open (2024-09-13).

what_it_is.value: awrit (Actual Web Rendering In Terminal): a full Chromium browser, run as Electron offscreen rendering, whose painted frames stream into a terminal that speaks the Kitty graphics protocol. It has a web-tech toolbar and Chrome extensions, and mouse and keyboard drive the page. The repo is archived; the author cites limited time and rising security issues, and points macOS users to cmux.
what_it_is.note: [measured] Archived flag confirmed with gh api repos/chase/awrit (archived: true). Electron ^37.3.1 is in package.json.

language.value: Rust 374 KB (mostly a vendored crossterm fork plus the napi native module awrit-native-rs), TypeScript 97 KB, JavaScript 31 KB. Runs on Electron 37 and Node ≥22.
language.note: [measured] Tree listing shows awrit-native-rs/crates/crossterm vendored. App logic lives in src/*.ts.

graphics_mechanism.value: Kitty graphics protocol only. Electron `offscreen: true` emits `paint` events carrying a BGRA bitmap. awrit converts it to RGBA, writes it to POSIX shared memory and transmits `f=32,t=s,a=T,C=1,q=2`. The fast path uses kitty animation: frame 1 is a paused container image, each webview paint loads as an animation frame (`a=f,r=N,X=1`), and that frame is composited into the visible one at the layout rect (`a=c,C=1,x,y,w,h`). At startup it probes three capabilities, 100 ms timeout each: load a 1×1 image (`f=24,t=d,i=4294111295`), load a frame (`a=f,r=2`), and composite (`a=c,C=1,r=2,c=1`). If frames or compose fail, a fallback re-sends the whole bitmap at a cell-plus-pixel offset (`X=,Y=`) on every paint. The code notes that Ghostty 'and probably most other terminals only support a very small subset'.
graphics_mechanism.note: [measured] Also read src/paint.ts and awrit-native-rs/crates/crossterm/src/terminal/sys/unix.rs (query_kitty_graphics_support).

where_it_draws.value: It fills the terminal window (or kitty split) it runs in. It clears the screen and places one image that covers the toolbar and content layout, and paints update that image in place. Nothing scrolls with text; Chromium does the page scrolling. Size comes from TIOCGWINSZ pixel dimensions (crossterm window_size). On Wayland under kitty, it reads the scale from ~/.config/monitors.xml.
where_it_draws.note: [measured] Clear-screen seen in src/index.ts setup(). Scale seen in src/dpi.ts.

input_model.value: The kitty keyboard protocol is a hard requirement. awrit pushes DISAMBIGUATE | REPORT_ALL_KEYS_AS_ESCAPE_CODES | REPORT_ALTERNATE_KEYS | REPORT_EVENT_TYPES and exits with 'Extended keyboard support is required' if the terminal refuses. For the mouse it enables 1000/1002/1003/1015/1006 plus SGR-Pixels 1016, so pointer events arrive in pixels. It divides them by devicePixelRatio, decides toolbar or content by y, and forwards them through Electron `webContents.sendInputEvent` (mouseDown/Up/Move, and mouseWheel with a ±100 delta). Keys go through the config.js keybindings first, then to the focused webContents as rawKeyDown/char/keyUp. Bracketed paste and focus events are on.
input_model.note: [measured] Also read awrit-native-rs/src/term.rs, awrit-native-rs/crates/crossterm/src/event.rs (EnableMouseCapture includes ?1016h) and src/index.ts.

activity.value: 1,382 stars · archived · pushed 2026-04-25 · latest release awrit-native-rs-2.0.3 (2025-08-25)

td_overlap.note: [inferred] A live web page as the content of a terminal pane matches TD's 'open an HTML brief in a split' goal. I left out same-stack on purpose: the Rust bytes are a vendored crossterm plus a napi shim, and the app itself is TypeScript on Electron.

steal_for_td.value: Implement kitty-graphics shared-memory transmission (t=s) plus animation-frame load and compose (a=f with r=; a=c with x,y,w,h,C=1), and answer awrit's three-step probe OK. Then every Chromium repaint becomes a dirty-rect composite into one resident image instead of a full-frame re-upload. Put awrit's three probe strings in TD's conformance test verbatim.
steal_for_td.note: [inferred]

trap.value: Don't copy awrit's architecture for TD's own HTML pane. It ships a whole Electron/Chromium, the author archived it over security issues, and every frame crosses shared memory as a full BGRA bitmap. TD already owns the GPU and can embed a web view directly. awrit matters only as a client TD should be able to host. Also, a terminal that answers a=q OK but lacks a=f/a=c pushes awrit onto the slow full-frame fallback, so answer each frame probe truthfully.
trap.note: [inferred]

what_it_is.value: Browsh: a text-based browser backed by real headless Firefox. A web extension serialises each page's text and pixel colours, and a Go 'interfacer' renders them in a TTY or serves them over HTTP to other browsers. It targets low-bandwidth SSH/Mosh browsing while keeping modern JavaScript support.
what_it_is.note: [measured]

language.value: JavaScript 111 KB (Firefox web extension) and Go 108 KB (tcell TUI 'interfacer'). Needs Firefox installed.

graphics_mechanism.value: Unicode half-blocks, no graphics protocol. The web extension takes two screenshots of the visible DOM, one with text hidden and one with text drawn in a full-block glyph font, and samples background and text colours from them. On the Go side, a cell holding text shows the real DOM character in its colour. Any other cell becomes '▄', with the background colour as the top 'pixel' and the foreground as the bottom one: 2 vertical pixels per cell, in 24-bit colour via tcell.
graphics_mechanism.note: [measured] See buildCell(), commented 'This is where we implement the UTF8 half-block trick', and webext/src/dom/graphics_builder.js.

where_it_draws.value: A fullscreen tcell screen with a tab/URL bar on top. The page is a scrolled viewport that is re-rendered on every scroll; yScroll is doubled when sent back to Firefox because each cell holds two pixel rows. Nothing lands in scrollback.
where_it_draws.note: [inferred] Viewport and scroll behaviour read in tty.go handleMouseScroll. Alternate-screen use is assumed from tcell's default.

input_model.value: tcell with EnableMouse. A click is translated to page coordinates (x + xScroll, y − uiHeight + yScroll) and sent as JSON to the web extension, which dispatches it into the DOM. The wheel scrolls the frame. Keys go to the page, except browsh's own chords: Ctrl+Q quit, Ctrl+L URL bar, Ctrl+T new tab, Ctrl+W close tab, Backspace back, arrows and PgUp/PgDn scroll.
input_model.note: [measured] From handleMouseEvent and handleUserKeyPress.

td_overlap.note: [inferred] It renders HTML pages as the content of a terminal pane. It is written in Go and JavaScript, so not same-stack.

steal_for_td.value: Keep a text layer under every rendered document. Browsh keeps page text as real characters in the grid and page graphics as pixels, by screenshotting with the text hidden. When TD renders a Markdown or HTML brief as pixels in a pane or float, it should also keep that brief's plain text addressable, so that TD's grep and pane_events tooling and its agents can read and search it. Pixels alone are invisible to them.
steal_for_td.note: [inferred]

trap.value: Half-block rendering caps a page at 2 vertical pixels per cell and loses glyph-level detail, and browsh hasn't shipped a release since January 2024. For a GPU terminal it is only a fallback for panes where TD's protocols go undetected (for example over nested SSH), not a model for TD's own HTML view.
trap.note: [inferred]

what_it_is.value: presenterm: a Rust tool that turns Markdown into terminal slideshows, with themes, layouts, speaker notes, executable code blocks and images. It also renders mermaid, d2, LaTeX and typst code blocks to images; mermaid goes through mermaid-cli, which starts a headless browser at about 2 s per image.
what_it_is.note: [measured] Mermaid detail from docs/src/features/code/mermaid.md.

language.value: Rust (about 99% of bytes)

graphics_mechanism.value: Supports iTerm2 inline images (OSC 1337, including multipart), Kitty graphics in two modes, Sixel, and ASCII half-blocks as the universal fallback. The kitty modes are 'local' (t=f, a temp-file path, preferred) and 'remote' (t=d, base64). Under tmux, kitty images use U=1 virtual placements and U+10EEEE placeholder cells, and GIFs play as kitty animation frames. Detection lives in src/terminal/capabilities.rs. It writes a 1×1 RGBA kitty `a=q` twice, once with t=f and once with t=d, followed by DA1 `CSI c` as a sentinel. It parses `_G` OK replies per image id, and the DA1 answer for sixel. If nothing answers, a watchdog thread sends DSR after about a second. It also probes kitty's text-sizing protocol: on the alt screen it writes `OSC 66;s=2; ` and `OSC 66;n=1:d=2; ` and reads back the cursor column. Mode order is iterm2 → kitty local → kitty remote → sixel → ascii. iterm2 is used only for terminals recognised by env (iTerm2, WezTerm, mintty, Konsole).
graphics_mechanism.note: [measured] Also read src/terminal/emulator.rs (preferred_protocol, is_detected) and src/terminal/image/protocols/kitty.rs.

where_it_draws.value: A fullscreen alternate screen, one slide at a time. Images are cell-anchored placements, sized as a percentage of terminal width (`![image:width:50%](x.png)`) and redrawn on each slide change. Nothing goes to scrollback.
where_it_draws.note: [inferred] Sizing syntax is measured from the docs. The alt-screen slide model is inferred from the app's shape and the EnterAlternateScreen use in capabilities.rs.

input_model.value: Keyboard only, through configurable `bindings`. Defaults: next l/j/→/PgDn/↓/space; previous h/k/←/PgUp/↑; n/p fast skip; gg/G first/last slide; <number>G go to slide; ? opens the bindings modal; Esc closes a modal; Ctrl+C or q exits; Ctrl+Z suspends.
input_model.note: [measured]

td_overlap.note: [inferred] It renders Markdown, the file type TD opens on Ctrl+click, inside a pane, and it is written in Rust.

steal_for_td.value: Answer the kitty query truthfully for each transmission medium. Support t=f (and t=t) as well as t=d: presenterm switches to 'local' mode whenever the t=f query succeeds, and then hands TD a file path instead of base64, which is the cheapest path for a terminal on the same machine. After that, implement OSC 66 text sizing. presenterm, glow (on main) and mcat (--md-kitty-headers) all probe for it to draw large Markdown headings.
steal_for_td.note: [inferred]

trap.value: Brand shortcuts hide what the terminal can actually do. If TD ever sets TERM_PROGRAM to a name presenterm recognises (WezTerm, say), presenterm switches to iTerm2 OSC 1337 without querying. And if nobody answers the probe, it falls back to ASCII blocks without saying so. Never impersonate another terminal's TERM or TERM_PROGRAM; answer the queries.
trap.note: [inferred]

what_it_is.value: Yazi: an async Rust terminal file manager with Lua plugins and built-in previews. Images are decoded and downscaled in-process, video thumbnails come from ffmpeg, PDF first pages from pdftoppm, and it also previews archives, code and directories. Markdown and HTML previews come from third-party plugins.
what_it_is.note: [measured] The pdftoppm and ffmpeg preview deps come from https://yazi-rs.github.io/docs/configuration/yazi.

language.value: Rust (about 94% of bytes), Lua (about 5%)

graphics_mechanism.value: Drivers in yazi-adapter: Kgp (kitty Unicode placeholders: `a=T,C=1,U=1`, then U+10EEEE plus row and column diacritics per cell); KgpOld (kitty classic: `a=t` transmit, then one placement per cell with `a=p,p=N,x,y,w,h,c=1,r=1,C=1`, so an image costs cols×rows placements); Iip (iTerm2 OSC 1337); Sixel; and fallbacks to Überzug++ (X11/Wayland overlay windows) and Chafa. Detection starts from the env brand and adds one probe burst: XTVERSION `CSI >q`; kitty `a=q,t=d` (id 278941603) and `a=q,t=s` over shared memory (id 916472805); `CSI 16t` for cell size; OSC 11 background; `CSI ?996n` colour scheme; DECRQM 12; DECRQSS cursor style; `CSI ?u`. DA1 `CSI 0c` closes the burst, with a 3 s timeout; if the brand is tmux, the burst is re-sent through passthrough. The brand (from TERM, TERM_PROGRAM, env vars, or an XTVERSION substring) selects the driver list: Kitty, Ghostty, Rio → Kgp; Konsole → KgpOld; iTerm2, WezTerm, VSCode, Tabby, Hyper, Bobcat → Iip then Sixel; foot, Windows Terminal, BlackBox → Sixel. An Unknown brand gets only what its probe proved: Sixel if DA1 contains 4, KgpOld if a=q returned OK, and never Unicode placeholders. If nothing is proven, x11 sessions get ueberzug X11, Wayland with a Hyprland/Sway/Niri/Wayfire socket gets ueberzug Wayland, and anything else gets chafa.
graphics_mechanism.note: [measured] Read yazi-emulator/src/{probe,brand,emulator}.rs, yazi-tty/src/sequence/query.rs, and yazi-adapter/src/drivers/{kgp,kgp_old,ueberzug}.rs.

where_it_draws.value: Cell-anchored placement inside its own preview pane in a fullscreen alt-screen TUI. Images are erased and redrawn whenever the preview changes or any UI element overlaps the shown rect (ClearInventory → image_erase), so they never scroll with text. The Überzug++ fallbacks draw overlay windows instead.

bubbles.note: Neither image protocol can reach TD's alacritty_terminal Handler today. Upstream vte sends ESC _ (APC, used by Kitty's `ESC _G`) to State::SosPmApcString and discards the bytes (vte src/lib.rs line 379). The vte ansi Performer's DCS `hook`/`put`, which Sixel's `DCS q` needs, are debug-log stubs (src/ansi.rs line 1311). So TD has three options: (a) a patched vte, as ayosec's `vte-graphics` 0.15.0 does; (b) a byte pre-filter in front of the parser that extracts APC G and DCS q, which then needs the cursor position and must emit the cursor moves itself; or (c) a different core such as rio-vt, which parses both natively.
bubbles.why: This is the single fact that decides how much of the graphics work touches TD's VT dependency. No approach avoids a parser change.

bubbles.note: TD already answers pixel-geometry queries correctly. app/src/host.rs handles TermEvent::TextAreaSizeRequest by formatting WindowSize{num_lines, num_cols, cell_width: geom.cell_width, cell_height: geom.cell_height} and writing the reply to the PTY. alacritty_terminal also fills TIOCSWINSZ ws_xpixel/ws_ypixel from those same cell sizes (tty/unix.rs lines 431-435). Kitty, Sixel and IIP clients size images from these numbers, so this prerequisite is already done. The only 8x16 and 8x20 hard-codes are in the socketpty test and the term.rs bench.
bubbles.why: It removes one prerequisite from TD's image plan, and it shows the host (server) side owns geometry, which is where the image store should live too.

bubbles.note: Queries a Kitty-graphics host must answer: (1) a=q query: reply `ESC _Gi=<id>;OK ESC \`, or `ENOENT:<msg>` or another error code. It must reply immediately and must not store the image. (2) Detection: clients send `ESC _Gi=31,s=1,v=1,a=q,t=d,f=24;AAAA ESC \` followed by `ESC [c`; the graphics reply arriving before the DA1 reply means supported. (3) Quiet modes q=1 (suppress OK) and q=2 (suppress errors too). (4) After a placement the cursor moves right by cols and down by rows unless C=1. (5) When over quota, delete images that have no placements first. (6) Deletes via a=d with d=i/p/z etc.; uppercase also frees the data.
bubbles.why: This is the minimum surface for a=q-probing clients (yazi, chafa, timg, kitty icat, ratatui-image) to pick TD up as a Kitty host.

bubbles.note: Unicode placeholders are the multiplexer-safe form of the Kitty protocol. The program creates a virtual placement (a=p,U=1), then prints U+10EEEE cells whose foreground colour encodes the image id (256-colour or 24-bit, with a third diacritic carrying the most significant byte) and whose combining diacritics encode row and column (U+0305 = 0, U+030D = 1, and so on). Anything that treats them as text (tmux, vim, TD's own server/client mirror) repositions the image for free. Support today: Ghostty (graphics_unicode.zig), iTerm2 3.7 (a placeholder fix is in the 3.7 notes), Rio (#1891/#1893, fixed 2026-08-24), and the ekollof cosmic-term fork (rowcol_diacritics.rs). WezTerm does not have it yet (PR #7924 open).
bubbles.why: Because the image rides in ordinary cells, TD's grid, selection, scrollback and client/server mirroring already carry it. This is likely the cheapest correct first Kitty feature for a multiplexing terminal.

bubbles.note: Queries a Sixel host must answer, as implemented in the ayosec fork and xterm.js: advertise Sixel in DA1 (the VT220+ '4' attribute; chrisduerr notes '4' means nothing while Alacritty reports VT102). Answer XTSMGRAPHICS `CSI ? Pi ; Pa ; Pv S` for Pi=1 (colour registers, 1024 in the fork) and Pi=2 (Sixel geometry, capped at 4096x4096; the fork answers via TextAreaSizeRequest). Honour DECSDM (DECSET/DECRST 80, Sixel display or scrolling mode) and choose the shared or private palette mode. Also answer CSI 14 t, 16 t and 18 t pixel and char size reports.
bubbles.why: Sixel clients (chafa, notcurses, mpv vo=sixel, lsix) probe these before drawing. A missing or incorrect reply makes them fall back to half-block characters.

bubbles.note: The Good Image Protocol (Contour, experimental) is the only protocol here designed around compositing layers and named pools. Upload with `DCS u n=<name>,f=<fmt>;!<b64> ST`, render with `DCS r n=<name>,c=<cols>,r=<rows> ST`, release with `DCS d n=<name> ST`. Layers are below, replace and above; the pool uses LRU eviction; it advertises as DA1 code 90. `contour cat` is the reference client. The spec repo has 36 stars and last pushed 2026-04-12, so nobody but Contour has adopted it.
bubbles.why: Named images and explicit layers map neatly onto TD's own 'floating square' idea, but adoption is effectively zero, so it is a design reference, not a protocol to implement.

bubbles.note: kitty's `launch --type=os-panel` creates an OS window 'as a desktop panel' (layer-shell on Wayland). These are kitty's native equivalents of TD's 'floating square' and 'split pane' targets, reached from open-actions.
bubbles.why: It shows kitty already offers the three destinations TD is designing (overlay over the pane, split, and a panel outside the terminal) behind one launch verb.

bubbles.note: Stock alacritty_terminal can't host any subject in this cluster yet, because its VT parser (vte master, v0.15) drops the sequences they rely on. ESC _ (0x5F) goes into SosPmApcString and the bytes are discarded, so kitty `ESC_G…` graphics never reach the Handler. DCS hook/unhook are logged as unhandled, so no Sixel. DA1 answers `CSI ?6c`, which lacks attribute 4, so nobody detects sixel. CSI t handles only 14 (text-area pixels) and 18 (chars), with no 16t for cell size. There is no XTVERSION (`CSI >q`) handler. The kitty keyboard protocol sits behind a `kitty_keyboard` config flag, and awrit exits without it. TD needs a parser patch or a byte-stream pre-filter for APC/DCS before any client-side detection matters.
bubbles.why: This decides TD's first engineering slice. Every client in the cluster detects kitty with an APC `a=q` query, sixel with DA1 attribute 4, and cell size with 14t/16t or TIOCGWINSZ.

bubbles.note: Conformance checklist, taken from the detection code of yazi, euporie, presenterm, awrit, ueberzugpp, tdf, w3m and glow. TD should answer each of these promptly and truthfully: DA1 `CSI c` (include 4 only if sixel is real); XTVERSION `CSI >q` (yazi maps the substring to a brand); `CSI 14t`, `CSI 16t`, `CSI 18t`; XTSMGRAPHICS `CSI ?1;1;0S` and `CSI ?2;1;0S`; kitty `ESC_G a=q` with each medium, t=d, t=f and t=s (presenterm asks t=f and t=d separately, yazi t=d and t=s); awrit's frame probes `a=f,r=2` and `a=c,C=1,r=2,c=1`; OSC 10/11/12/4 `?`; `CSI ?996n`; DECRQM `CSI ?1016$p` and `CSI ?12$p`; DECRQSS `ESC P $q q ESC \`; `CSI ?u`; DSR `CSI 5n` and `CSI 6n`; and the OSC 66 cursor-advance probe. TIOCGWINSZ must carry per-pane ws_xpixel/ws_ypixel, because ueberzugpp, mcat, tdf and w3m read it before any escape.
bubbles.why: One test list, sourced from real clients, becomes TD's acceptance test for 'programs can show pixels', and each line traces back to a client that breaks without it.

bubbles.note: Consolidated list of the queries TD must answer for these clients to pick pixels (measured from source). DA1 'CSI c' or 'CSI 0c': include 4 only if Sixel works (notcurses, ratatui-image, timg, viuer and chafa all key Sixel on it; notcurses discards XTSMGRAPHICS answers without it and hangs if DA1 is missing). Kitty 'ESC _Gi=31,s=1,v=1,a=q,t=d,f=24;AAAA ST' must get exactly 'ESC _Gi=31;OK ST', before the DA1 reply (ratatui-image, viuer); notcurses sends 'ESC _Gi=1,a=q; ST' and accepts any _G reply; ratatui-image may add i=32 (o=z) and i=33 (t=s) probes. XTVERSION 'CSI >0q' or 'CSI >q' gets 'DCS >| name version ST' (notcurses, timg). XTGETTCAP 'DCS +q544e;524742;687061 ST' (TN, RGB, hpa; notcurses). Size: CSI 14t (text area in px, reply CSI 4;h;w t), CSI 16t (cell px, reply CSI 6;h;w t), CSI 18t (cells), plus correct ws_xpixel/ws_ypixel in TIOCGWINSZ, which is mpv's ONLY source and a fallback for timg and ratatui-image. XTSMGRAPHICS 'CSI ?2;1;0S', 'CSI ?1;1;0S', 'CSI ?1;3;256S' (notcurses). OSC 10/11 '?' and OSC 4 palette queries; DECRQM 'CSI ?2026$p' and 'CSI ?1016$p'; Kitty keyboard 'CSI ?u'; 'CSI 6n' and 'CSI 5n' sentinels (reply 'CSI 0n'). Clients that pick Kitty only by name, whatever TD answers: chafa (env term DB), timg (TERM or XTVERSION substring). Those need upstream entries.
bubbles.why: This is the host-side contract for the whole cluster in one place; it can become TD's capability-reply test fixture.

bubbles.note: Same-stack gap, measured in alacritty's own code (alacritty/vte master at abeae76, alacritty/alacritty master): (1) vte's Parser sends 'ESC _' (APC) to State::SosPmApcString and drops every byte with no Perform callback, so Kitty graphics never reach alacritty_terminal. (2) vte's ansi Performer implements hook/put/unhook as 'unhandled' debug logs, so a Sixel DCS is dropped too. (3) CSI t handles only 14, 18, 22 and 23; CSI 16t (cell size) is unhandled. No XTVERSION ('CSI > q') handler. (4) alacritty_terminal answers DA1 with 'ESC[?6c' (no 4, so no Sixel) and DA2 with 'ESC[>0;version;1c'. (5) CSI 14t goes out as Event::TextAreaSizeRequest, which the embedder must answer. TD therefore needs a byte pre-parser, or a patched vte, in front of alacritty_terminal for APC and DCS, and its own replies for DA1, XTVERSION, 16t and XTSMGRAPHICS.
bubbles.why: This is the single biggest implementation fact for TD's pixels phase, and it applies equally to Zed's terminal (cluster A).

bubbles.note: alacritty_terminal's tty sets ws_xpixel = ws_col * cell_width and ws_ypixel = ws_row * cell_height as integer c_ushort (tty/unix.rs ToWinsize for WindowSize). TD must pass real cell pixel sizes in WindowSize on every resize. gpui cell widths are fractional, so truncating to integers makes the pixel size clients compute drift from the real grid by up to one pixel per column across a wide pane (this last part is [inferred], not measured).
bubbles.why: mpv sizes video only from these fields; timg and ratatui-image fall back to them; a zero or wrong value silently gives 320x240 video or misaligned images.
